strongest_angle: Examine the November 2026 Scientific American report and arXiv study detailing how quantum researchers proved that no material can be completely transparent due to the quantum decay of photons into phonons.

key_facts.fact: The Guinness Book of World Records lists Ivan Smalyukh as the inventor of the most transparent material known, developed at his lab at the University of Colorado Boulder.

Physicists Angelo Esposito, Alberto Nicolis, and Federico Piazza published a preprint on arXiv on October 8, 2026, arguing that quantum decay of photons into phonons makes complete transparency impossible.

In a mathematically perfect superfluid, a light beam could travel a distance equal to the diameter of Earth before fading noticeably according to research discussed in Yahoo News on November 13, 2026.
Gels developed by Ivan Smalyukh's lab at the University of Colorado Boulder become significantly light-absorbing if a layer about 30 cm thick is applied, as reported by News.KG on November 12, 2026.
